The Sheriff's Office collects tax bills, the PVA assesses, and the County Clerk takes over after April 15. All three work near the Greenup County Courthouse in the town of Greenup. The Property Valuation Administrator is in Room 209 at 301 Main Street, open Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

Mail to the sheriff goes to PO Box 318, Greenup, KY 41144. The sheriff's tax page takes online payments with your bill number and mailing address. The processor, not the sheriff, keeps the convenience fee added to an online payment. Refunds and account problems are handled in person at the sheriff's office, and staff do not process them by phone.

sections.h2: What a bill costs after April 15
sections.html:
Any bill left unpaid when April 15 arrives leaves the sheriff for the County Clerk, and the amount owed begins to rise. That date is the final one for paying at the Sheriff's Office. Bills turned over to the Clerk pick up fees that the original bill never showed, and the sheriff's page cites House Bill 262 as the reason for the April 15 date.

The state's worked example follows a bill through the stages, and each one costs more than the last: payment within five business days of transfer, payment after the county attorney's first notice, a second month of interest in May, newspaper advertising in June, and finally purchase by a third-party buyer at the sale. The example assumes a 4 percent sheriff commission, so your actual figures depend on the local rate.

Once a certificate exists, 1 percent interest is added each month. The sheriff's site keeps links to earlier bills for tax years 2015 through 2019, which helps when you trace an old balance. The Clerk's sale of delinquent bills must fall 90 to 135 days after the transfer, which in a normal year means July 14 to August 28. If you hold a bill that reaches the sale, ask the Clerk's office for the third-party purchaser rules.

Begin at the PVA, because Kentucky lets only owners who held a conference take a case to the board. Every property is revalued each year and physically examined at least once every four years, so a value can move even when your house has not changed.

  • Conferences happen while the roll is open in May, a 13-day window starting the first Monday. Staff can meet earlier once notices are mailed.
  • Then file with the County Clerk before the office closes on the next business day.
  • The board convenes four to five weeks after inspection ends and sits at most five days unless the state agrees to more.
  • Bring documents the board can weigh: building costs, insurance policies, listings and photos. No documents, no reduction.

Taxes equal assessment times rate, so if the rate holds, a higher value means a higher bill and a lower value a lower one. Rates come from the county, city and school boards, not the PVA. Keep your mailing address current with the PVA, and never treat a missing bill or notice as a reason to skip payment.

A resident owner who is 65 or older, or totally disabled, has $49,100 taken off the assessed value for 2025 and 2026.

Show the PVA a birth certificate, license or passport to prove age. Disability claims use other documents, so ask which ones and how often the claim renews. The office can also tell you the current savings on your own parcel.

Ask each office for a payoff, because which office holds the bill depends on the date. Before April 15 it sits with the sheriff. Afterward the Clerk has it, and the Clerk's delinquent tax page links purchaser information and the application.

The January 1 owner owes the year's tax. Under KRS 134.420, a delinquent lien can trail the house for as long as 11 years after it sells. A buyer's title search will find a lien that has not been released, and a recording and release fee comes with clearing it.

Your closing agent will work out how the current bill is divided between you and the buyer. Any bill still open at the Clerk should be paid from your proceeds. A written payoff from the Clerk shows the full price of clearing title on a house with several years behind. If back taxes are piling up and repairs are not affordable, a cash buyer who takes the house as is can close on a short timeline and settle the liens at the table.

sections.h2: Paying the bill step by step
sections.html:
Start by finding the bill. If it has not come, the sheriff's office is the place to ask, and you will want your bill number and mailing address ready. Pay at the counter, by mail to the PO Box, or online. Online payment is quick but adds a processing fee, and the sheriff cannot waive it.

Keep the receipt or confirmation. A title company asking for proof that the year is paid is the most common reason to need it. If you overpay or a mistake shows up on your account, go to the sheriff's office in person, since that is the only way refunds and account fixes are handled.

When the sale is close, tell the PVA about the new owner's mailing address if the deed does not already carry it, so the next bill reaches the right person.

Greenup County lies along the Ohio River in the northeast corner of Kentucky, in the Huntington-Ashland metropolitan area. Greenup is the county seat and Flatwoods is the largest city. The July 2025 estimate was 35,213 residents, 2.1 percent fewer than the 2020 base. Owners live in 80.3 percent of housing, spread over 14,739 households, and the median home is valued at $134,000. Median owner costs are $1,186 a month with a mortgage and $483 without, and median gross rent is $860.

Most sellers here own a modest, long-held house, and the figures above suggest that taxes are a manageable cost. Still, a bill that slips past April 15 can complicate a listing, because the buyer's lender and title company will want the lien cleared before funds change hands. Checking the account early gives you time to fix a problem.

US 23 follows the river through Russell, Flatwoods, Raceland, Wurtland, Greenup and South Shore, which makes those river towns the busiest part of the market.

faqs.q: Where is Greenup County property tax paid?
faqs.a: At the Greenup County Sheriff's Office through April 15, in person, by mail to PO Box 318, Greenup, KY 41144, or online. Call (606) 473-9833. Processors charge convenience fees on online payments.

faqs.q: Which office explains a Greenup County assessment?
faqs.a: The PVA at (606) 473-9984, in Room 209 of the courthouse, 301 Main Street, with weekday hours of 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

faqs.q: What changes on April 15 in Greenup County?
faqs.a: The sheriff hands every unpaid bill to the County Clerk, which adds fees the original bill never showed. Call (606) 473-7394 for the total.

faqs.q: What is the Greenup County homestead amount?
faqs.a: The 2025 and 2026 figure is $49,100 off assessed value, open to owners 65 or older or totally disabled.

faqs.q: Will the Greenup County sheriff refund money by phone?
faqs.a: No. Refunds and account corrections must be requested in person at the office.
